question.problem: Kevin is moving his car in a straight line. His position relative to a fixed origin $O$ is given by the function $x(t)=2{e}^{t/2}\,\text{m},$ where $t$ is the time in seconds. Find its average position between $2$ and $6$ seconds.
question.worked_solution:
To calculate the average value of the position on $[{t}_{1},{t}_{2}],$ we use the average value formula

$$
{x}_{\text{avg}}=\frac{1}{{t}_{2}-{t}_{1}}\,{\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}x(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

So, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{6-2}\,{\int }_{2}^{6}2{e}^{t/2}\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot {2\cdot 2({e}^{t/2})|}_{2}^{6} \\  & ={e}^{6/2}-{e}^{2/2} \\  & ={e}^{3}-e.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the average position is $({e}^{3}-e)\,\text{m}.$
